next_question: Can Fix3 (_is_protocol_only_prefix) be redesigned to reject only truly protocol-only prefixes (no '/' in rest) without blocking valid host?query parameterization, and can a discriminating test demonstrate its independent necessity over Fix2?
why_next: This experiment resolves the parent MEASUREMENT_INVALID blocker (V1_HTTP_DESIGN_IMPOSSIBLE_IDS) and demonstrates real HTTP binding correctness 9/9 on valid IDs, expanding the claim ceiling. However, the frozen decision rule fails on C4 (B_UNFIXED_PROTOCOL_ONLY) because Fix3 is redundant with Fix2 for the tested URL pair and overbroad for host?query patterns (audit V1, V2). Fix3 necessity is not demonstrated, and Fix3 blocks valid parameterization. The next step should either redesign Fix3 to be non-redundant and non-overbroad with a discriminating test, or pivot to orthogonal high-upside question such as PUT/POST method fidelity or end-to-end economics.
